**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. English Language 3 (0730), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2025. Paper 3: Section A - Summary Writing; Section B - Text Reconstruction; Section C - Editing. Duration: two and a quarter hours.**

ALL THE QUESTIONS ARE COMPULSORY. THEY CARRY EQUAL MARKS.

Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or to number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks.

Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure of your identity will be considered as an attempt to cheat and will earn you a penalty.

In the SUMMARY WRITING question, use mainly your own words. Indiscriminate copying of portions of the passage as your answer will earn you no marks.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.
incertitudes: Page de garde : « Duration: Two and a Quarter Hours » (soit 2h15), « ALL THE QUESTIONS ARE COMPULSORY. THEY CARRY EQUAL MARKS ». Aucune règle de choix : `regles_choix` est vide dans les 3 fichiers, car les trois sections sont obligatoires.

Points : chaque section est imprimée « (15 MARKS) », soit 45 au total ; aucun écart constaté. Aucun corrigé officiel ni barème détaillé n'est imprimé : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées pour ce lot et la répartition interne des 15 points de chaque question est une hypothèse de correction.

Editing : le sujet ne dit pas combien de fautes il contient ; le corrigé en relève 18 (4 de structure, 14 de langue), comptées par script. La liste est celle qu'un correcteur attentif relèverait ; elle n'est pas le barème imprimé (inexistant). Les faits de structure (adresse, date, formule d'appel, paragraphes, formule finale) sont relevés parce que la consigne demande de soigner « language and structure ».

La mise en page imprimée (adresse « Kurumanjang City » et « Ola Keng » alignées à droite, formule finale « Faithfully Yours, Ola » alignée à droite) est rendue par des retours à la ligne ; l'alignement n'est pas conservé. L'exposant de « 14<sup>th</sup> » est rendu en HTML.

Le choix « Yours lovingly » comme formule finale est un choix de correction (lettre d'amour) ; « Yours sincerely » ou « Yours » seraient aussi défendables. « Mrs Eposi » : correction retenue « Eposi » ou « Miss Eposi » (le sujet ne dit pas si Eposi est mariée).

**SECTION C: EDITING (15 MARKS)**

**Read through this letter carefully and edit it, paying attention to language and structure.**

Kurumanjang City  
Ola Keng

Eposi my dear

How are you doing today? I am writing to express the strong love I have for you especially this 14<sup>th</sup> February. Mrs Eposi, you are different form plenty girls because your beauty is unspeakable and your voice always melts my heart and make it to skip a bit. Eposi, on this day, I offer you my heart as a Valentine's Gift praying that the almighty will be blessing you and keep you alife for me. You don't know how much I care for you because if you know, you will not be sleeping one day without calling. Bye for now.

Faithfully Yours,  
Ola
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Edited letter** (corrected text; 18 faults are listed below: 4 of structure and 14 of language)

Kurumanjang City,  
14th February

My dear Eposi,

How are you doing today? I am writing to express the strong love I have for you, especially on this 14th of February.

Eposi, you are different from many other girls because your beauty is indescribable and your voice always melts my heart and makes it skip a beat. On this day, I offer you my heart as a Valentine's gift, praying that the Almighty will bless you and keep you alive for me.

You don't know how much I care for you because, if you knew, you would not sleep one day without calling me. Bye for now.

Yours lovingly,  
Ola

**Fault-by-fault correction**

| No. | Type | Original | Correction | Rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Structure | Kurumanjang City / Ola Keng (top right) | Kurumanjang City, then the date (14th February) | The heading of an informal letter gives the writer's address and the date; the writer's name belongs in the signature, not in the address block, and the date is missing. |
| 2 | Structure | Eposi my dear | My dear Eposi, | Standard order of an affectionate salutation (My dear + name) followed by a comma. |
| 3 | Structure | one block of text | three short paragraphs | Opening and purpose, expression of feeling and the gift and prayer, then the closing: a letter is divided into paragraphs. |
| 4 | Structure | Faithfully Yours, | Yours lovingly, | "Yours faithfully" closes a letter that begins "Dear Sir/Madam"; a love letter needs an affectionate close, and only the first word takes a capital. |
| 5 | Language | especially this 14th February | especially on this 14th of February | A date needs the preposition "on" (and "of" is usual in "14th of February"). |
| 6 | Language | Mrs Eposi | Eposi (or Miss Eposi) | Register and meaning: "Mrs" marks a married woman and is stiff in a love letter; the name alone is enough. |
| 7 | Language | form | from | Spelling ("different from"). |
| 8 | Language | plenty girls | many other girls | "Plenty" is followed by "of" (plenty of girls); "many" is the usual quantifier with a countable noun, and "other" makes the comparison clear. |
| 9 | Language | unspeakable | indescribable | "Unspeakable" means too bad to be spoken of; for beauty the right word is "indescribable" (or "beyond description"). |
| 10 | Language | make | makes | Subject-verb agreement: the subject "your voice" is singular and the verb is coordinated with "melts". |
| 11 | Language | make it to skip | make it skip (makes it skip) | After "make" + object, the bare infinitive is used, without "to". |
| 12 | Language | a bit | a beat | Fixed idiom: a heart "skips a beat". |
| 13 | Language | Valentine's Gift | Valentine's gift | Capital letters: "gift" is a common noun. |
| 14 | Language | the almighty | the Almighty | "Almighty" used for God takes a capital letter. |
| 15 | Language | will be blessing | will bless | Wrong tense: a wish or prayer takes the simple form "will bless" (or "may ... bless"), and it must be parallel to "keep". |
| 16 | Language | alife | alive | Spelling. |
| 17 | Language | if you know, you will not be sleeping | if you knew, you would not sleep | Unreal (second) conditional: past simple in the if-clause and "would" + base verb in the main clause; the continuous form does not suit a habit. |
| 18 | Language | without calling. | without calling me. | The verb "call" needs its object "me". |

**Marking grid (15 marks).** The paper prints only the total and asks the candidate to pay attention to "language and structure". The faults above are those a careful editor finds; a candidate is rewarded for each fault correctly found and corrected (structure of the letter and language), for not introducing new errors, and for a clean, well presented edited copy. The exact allocation of the 15 marks is not printed.

**Common mistakes**

1. Correcting only the spelling ("form", "alife") and ignoring the structure of the letter (heading, date, salutation, paragraphs, complimentary close).
2. Rewriting the whole letter in different words: editing means correcting the faults while keeping the writer's meaning and as much of the original wording as possible.
3. Correcting "will be blessing" or "if you know" without changing the other half of the sentence ("keep", "will not be sleeping"), so that the tenses still do not match.
